classification.difficultyReason: Compare intercepts, turning points and tail directions to identify axis reflections and reflection in both axes.

content.prompt:
The leftmost diagram shows a sketch of $y=f(x)$.
Determine the transformation $y=-f(x)$, $y=f(-x)$, $y=-f(-x)$ for each of these graphs.

spec.description: Qualitative reference curve with no grid. Compact width preserves the meaningful four-figure comparison row; final-size label readability requires review.
spec.mathematics: Crosses at (-1,0) and (0,1), has a local minimum at (1,0), a local maximum left of the y-axis, and lower-left and upper-right tails. Bezier control coordinates describe qualitative shape only and are not additional givens.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied graph features remain visible in questions.

spec.description: Exact horizontal reflection of the reference Bezier curve, including every control point.
spec.mathematics: Touches the x-axis at (-1,0), crosses at (1,0) and (0,1), and has upper-left and lower-right tails.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph visible; transformation answer withheld.

answer.worked: Reflection across the $y$-axis sends $(x,y)$ to $(-x,y)$. The touching point $(1,0)$ becomes $(-1,0)$, while the $y$-intercept stays at $(0,1)$. Hence $y=f(-x)$.

spec.description: Exact vertical reflection of the reference Bezier curve, including every control point.
spec.mathematics: Crosses at (-1,0) and (0,-1), touches the x-axis at a local maximum (1,0), and has upper-left and lower-right tails.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph visible; transformation answer withheld.

answer.worked: Reflection across the $x$-axis sends $(x,y)$ to $(x,-y)$. The $x$-intercepts stay fixed and $(0,1)$ becomes $(0,-1)$. Hence $y=-f(x)$.

spec.description: Exact reflection in both axes of the reference Bezier curve, including every control point.
spec.mathematics: Touches the x-axis at a local maximum (-1,0), crosses at (1,0) and (0,-1), and has lower-left and upper-right tails.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph visible; transformation answer withheld.

answer.worked: Reflection across both axes sends $(x,y)$ to $(-x,-y)$. The touching point $(1,0)$ becomes $(-1,0)$ and $(0,1)$ becomes $(0,-1)$. Hence $y=-f(-x)$, equivalent to a $180^\circ$ rotation about the origin.
